tools.name: list_surface_contracts
tools.description: List the platform surface contracts published in Penny's free registry, with claim counts.

tools.name: get_surface_contract
tools.description: Get the machine-readable surface contract for a platform host (read/write semantics, pending states, rate limits, limits, idempotency, pagination completeness, data portability), each claim carrying its evidence and its verification status.

tools.name: verify_surface
tools.description: Run the anonymous conformance checks for a contract now and return verified / failed / unknown / manual / unsupported per claim.

tools.name: contribute_discrepancy
tools.description: Report a platform behaviour that contradicts a published claim, or a new claim, with evidence. Stored as pending; a published contract is never changed without independent verification.

tools.name: get_integration_recipe
tools.description: Get a plain-text integration recipe for a platform: the order of operations to use it, and a guard clause for every behaviour we measured going wrong, each naming the contract claim behind it. Derived from the contract, so it cannot drift from it.

name: preflight_mcp_server
description: Run the anonymous MCP handshake against ANY https MCP endpoint you name, right now, and get back a verdict (open / refused / unreachable / initialize-transport-error), the shape of any refusal body, whether the server is stateful (sets Mcp-Session-Id), how many tools tools/list returns, and the guar

name: prepay_check
description: Check an x402 route BEFORE you pay it. GET /v1/prepay?url=<the route> makes ONE unpaid GET with no payment header and no credential, and returns one row: the measured HTTP status, the parsed x402 v2 challenge (scheme / network / asset / amount / payTo), whether that challenge is schema-valid exact-o

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "preflight_mcp_server" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contribute_discrepancy, preflight_mcp_server, prepay_check · Private data: preflight_mcp_server, prepay_check · Public sink: contribute_discrepancy · Destructive: verify_surface, preflight_mcp_server.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contribute_discrepancy, preflight_mcp_server, prepay_check · Private data: preflight_mcp_server, prepay_check · Public sink: contribute_discrepancy · Destructive: verify_surface, preflight_mcp_server

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "contribute_discrepancy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Report a platform behaviour that contradicts a published claim, or a new claim, with evidence. Stored as pending; a published contract is never changed without independent verification." → after: "Report a platform behaviour that contradicts a published claim, or a new claim, with evidence. One-line call: POST /v1/contribute with {contractId, kind, statement, evidence[], reporter, observedAt}. Stored as pending; a published contract is never changed without independent verification. A contrac"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
